scope_notes.label: Argo seasonal envelope and dateline scope
scope_notes.source_locator: Publisher abstract, Plain Language Summary and Data Availability Statement.
scope_notes.summary: Source preview reports a spring envelope from 150 E to 170 W and an autumn extension to 140 W. These dateline-crossing spans are not traced current lengths. Spring latitude limits are not paired current edges; full methods, averaging years and calendar months remain unresolved.

scope_notes.label: WOA01 mean flow and seasonal anomaly separation
scope_notes.summary: Full 2004 paper distinguishes surface and 0-200 m WOA01 geostrophy relative to 1500 dbar, modeled Sverdrup flow, and band-passed seasonal anomaly sections at 170 E. Anomaly zero contours and averaging windows cannot define current widths or endpoints. Numerical compatible flow fields remain needed.

widths.boundary_rule: Author-reported geostrophic current width; exact velocity cutoff, paired lateral coordinates and reference level not specified in the inspected descriptor. Direct equatorial meters referenced to 500 m are a different method.
widths.extraction_method: Range transcribed from visually reviewed original prose. No source figure or velocity boundaries digitized.
widths.geographic_scope: 170 E meridional sections, geostrophic SECC near 10 S. Excludes South Tropical Countercurrent south of 15 S and the subsurface/equatorial Cromwell extensions.
widths.layer: Author geostrophic-current envelope with broad vertical support; exact width depth and reference level unresolved. Speeds above 10 cm/s generally within upper 300 m is a separate statement, not a 0–300 m width slab.
widths.name: Pacific South Equatorial Countercurrent

original_regional_context.display_aria_label: Pacific SECC near 10 S at 170 E: source-reported historical 300 to 900 km width range. No midpoint, annual extrema, paired mapped boundaries or numerical uncertainty supplied.
original_regional_context.display_caption: Near 10 S at 170 E: 300–900 km geostrophic-current width description from the 1965–1968 cruise study. The range endpoints are not assigned to individual cruise dates; no midpoint or annual range inferred.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: This SECC is distinct from the deeper equatorial/subsurface extensions and the South Tropical Countercurrent south of 15 S. Width layer, geostrophic reference level and paired boundary criterion remain unresolved. The upper-300 m speed statement and direct current-meter 500 m reference are separate descriptors.
original_regional_context.display_title: Historical Pacific SECC width range at 170 E
original_regional_context.quality_note: Complete original report inspected. Repeated historical geostrophic sections support an author width range; raw boundary calculations and endpoint occupations were not recovered.
